messages.author: 17ebe6096d5db61f
messages.subject: Controlling panel sizes directly
parts:
Hadley made multiple references to improving the layout system over
the course of 2009, generally in reference to the ability to directly
specify core graph (panel) sizes, rather than controlling sizes
indirectly just by specifying the viewport dimensions.

Most recently, in November:

> it's on my to do list as part of a rewrite of the layout system.

Has anything come of this?

I need to control the plot area dimensions (not the overall figure
bounding dimensions) for printed figures. In my specific case,
generating a set of separate plots of equivalent size for a paper is
confounded because some have Y axis labels in the single digits, while
others are in the double digits, and this width difference is enough
to change the width of the core panel areas between different plots
with otherwise identical settings and identical dimensions given to
ggsave. I love ggplot, but for my usage (publication output, not just
interactive visualization) this is proving the biggest gotcha.

It is proving extremely challenging to work around at a lower level
(direct grid/grob manipulation).

Thanks.
